quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep going at your current speed.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when it is safe.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be careful. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane that is closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane closest to the left curb.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way when turning.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet behind them. Never follow closely behind a large vehicle. The driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, gates, or flashing lights tell you to. Some crossings do not have these devices. Never drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to keep right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the road:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Slow down and pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Press the brakes hard and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Don't use the brakes until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: When you see a yield sign, you must let other traffic go first if they are close enough to cause a problem. You should be ready to stop, but you can keep going if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or people who do not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, what should you check?

options.text: Only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Keep going at the same speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Park parallel to the edge. On one-way streets, move to the edge closest to you.

questions.question: Which of these can distract drivers and increase crash risk?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving can distract you and increase the chance of a crash.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which of these situations?

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass only if it is safe and does not block other traffic.

questions.question: When driving in fog, should you use your high beam headlights?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Only the right lane can pass.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean:

options.text: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders when it is safe and the other lane is clear.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires improve your vehicle's grip on icy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other slippery conditions. Winter driving is harder and requires extra caution. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires help your car grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to rejoin the main road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to return to the main road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts drivers to a winding road ahead. These signs are usually yellow with black markings. Slow down and be prepared for curves.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill without a curb, also turn toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn toward the center so your car rolls into the curb.
